solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Experiences a blow — it helps provide comfort in prayer

definitions.text: it helps provide comfort in prayer

parts.note: to experience something is to have it, so 'experiences' gives has
a sock is a punch, a blow

explanation.surface: Someone takes a knock and finds solace kneeling in church.
explanation.walkthrough: A hassock is a padded cushion for kneeling on in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is the kneeling cushion in a pew, easing the knees of worshippers during devotions.

clue.text: Hard master maltreated one often seen on treadmill

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: something maltreated is knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cruel master works a creature on a treadmill.
explanation.definitionFit: Pet hamsters famously run on exercise wheels in their cages, a treadmill of sorts.

clue.text: Daily broadcast that's illuminating, naturally

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
to beam is to transmit, broadcast

explanation.surface: A daily programme that sheds light on the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a ray of light from the sun, illumination from nature.

clue.text: Source of oil, as it happens

definitions.text: Source of oil, as it happens

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of oil
a live broadcast goes out as it happens

explanation.surface: A remark about where oil comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: the olive is a source of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is pressed from the fruit of the olive tree.

clue.text: Novel youngster dropped off

parts.note: a kid is a child
to drop off is to fall asleep, so napped

explanation.surface: A child was dropped off somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is the book by Robert Louis Stevenson.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapped is Robert Louis Stevenson's 1886 adventure story about David Balfour.

clue.text: Make rough version of a score before noon

indicators.note: says the anagram comes ahead of the next piece
a version of something is a reworking of it, so the letters of 'a score' are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An arranger roughs up a musical score before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks musical, but A SCORE is simply fodder: 'version of' rearranges it to COARSE, then N for noon follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To coarsen is to roughen in texture or manner, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Prison key on ring

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: C is a musical key
a link is a ring in a chain

explanation.surface: A jailer's key hangs on a key ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clink' is British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Clink is informal slang for a jail or lock-up.

clue.text: You can get trams, and Edam, here

definitions.text: You can get trams, and Edam, here

indicators.note: the answer can be got from these letters by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A tourist note on a Dutch city's trams and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place: Amsterdam has trams, and Edam cheese comes from nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital runs an extensive tram network and sells Edam, a cheese from a town close by.

clue.text: Speaker's supporter in fight after TV programme

indicators.note: says the word for fight comes after the programme

parts.note: a soap is a soap opera
to box is to fight

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out once a TV show ends.
explanation.walkthrough: A soapbox is the improvised platform of a street-corner orator.
explanation.definitionFit: A soapbox is a crate an orator stands on, so it bears up a public speaker.

clue.text: These characters aren't involved with us

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Some people simply aren't like us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people or letters but means temperaments.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their character or temperament.

clue.text: People generally good-natured on island

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece 'on' another comes after it

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
kind means good-natured

explanation.surface: Islanders are, on the whole, a kindly folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland; 'on' places KIND after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mankind is the human race, people taken collectively.

clue.text: Second of March?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in old business letters '...' (inst.) means of the current month, which would be March if written then

explanation.walkthrough: 'The 2nd inst.' in old correspondence means the second day of this month; the question mark admits March is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment of time is an instant, and the commercial abbreviation inst. denotes the current calendar month.

clue.text: European politician aboard the rescue craft in recreation area

indicators.note: being aboard a vessel puts one inside it, so the politician goes within the boat

parts.note: Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood
MEP is a Member of the European Parliament

explanation.surface: A Euro politician on Noah's boat ends up somewhere fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme park is an amusement ground with rides built around a theme, a place for leisure.

clue.text: Burning material at the end of three months

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a glowing piece of coal or wood in a dying fire

definitions.text: at the end of three months
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the letters that close SeptEMBER, NovEMBER and DecEMBER

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like a time span, but it describes the word itself: the shared ending of three month names.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing coal remnant in a fire is called an ember, and the same letters finish three autumn and winter months.

clue.text: Type of European city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the upright typeface, as opposed to italic

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as asking for some kind of city; instead 'Type' is a printing term and 'of European city' is an adjective for Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers call upright lettering roman, and anything from Rome is Roman.

clue.text: What Canadian provinces do, in place of political leader

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ... Downing Street, the British prime minister's residence

explanation.walkthrough: Canada has ten provinces, so they 'number ten'; Number Ten is the London home of the UK prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The count of Canadian provinces is ten, and the prime minister's official London residence is 10 Downing Street.

clue.text: Soldier solves about ten logical puzzles, apparently

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for solves wraps the ten

parts.note: to do a puzzle is to solve it, so 'solves' gives does
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A paratrooper cracks ten brainteasers, or seems to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solves' is a verb in the surface and stays one: to do a crossword is to solve it. A paradox only appears contradictory, which is why 'apparently' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradox is a statement that seems self-contradictory yet may be true, a logical puzzle only in appearance.

clue.text: Unusually broad forward creating obstruction, in a way

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of broad set out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
a lock is a forward in rugby, playing in the second row of the scrum

explanation.surface: A burly rugby player blocks the way.
explanation.walkthrough: A lock is a rugby forward; the way is a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadblock is a barrier across a street, an obstruction in a road.

clue.text: After service, male assistant put back TV etc.

indicators.note: says the following pieces come after the word for service

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: put back means the word for assistant is read from end to start

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: After church, a man's helper puts the television back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'etc.' widens TV to all mass communication, so the definition covers press and radio too.
explanation.definitionFit: Television, radio and newspapers together form the media reaching a mass audience.

clue.text: Killer charged in Spain

parts.note: suggests a murderer on trial; really the bullfighter whom the bull charges in the Spanish ring

explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests an accused criminal, but it is the bull that charges at this killer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish bullfighting the bullfighter who kills the bull faces its charges.

clue.text: Part of same issue is raised by flashy articles

indicators.note: says the two pieces sit side by side
in a down clue, raising a word turns it upwards, so is reads backwards

parts.note: bling is showy jewellery

explanation.surface: A problem raised about showy jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring, not a problem; 'raised' turns IS upwards to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother or sister is one of the same parents' offspring, issue in the legal sense.

clue.text: Indicated average temperature

parts.note: the mean is an average

explanation.surface: A weather report showing the average temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: To have meant something is to have signified or pointed to it.

clue.text: Article, so minute, with tiny cover — amazing!

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: a cover goes round what it protects, so the word for tiny wraps the others

parts.note: wee means tiny
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation about something minuscule with an even smaller lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like an adjective meaning tiny, but it is M, the abbreviation; SO and M go inside WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome is an informal exclamation of admiration meaning wonderful or terrific.

clue.text: Closed count, coming to 100%

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
a tally is a count

explanation.surface: A final count comes to a full hundred per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' as an adverb means shut, as in 'pull the door to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally means completely, entirely, so one hundred per cent.

clue.text: Carpenter's construction accomplished after short time

indicators.note: says the word for accomplished comes after the time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
able means skilled, accomplished

explanation.surface: A carpenter finishes the job after a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is typical woodwork, a piece of furniture made by a joiner.

clue.text: Prohibition making some Stateside barmen testy

indicators.note: making some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Prohibition in the US left bar staff irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Debarment is the act of excluding or banning, a formal prohibition.

clue.text: He's enjoyed a long partnership in local match, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means a word spoken aloud, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: a derby is a game between local rivals; in British speech it is said like the answer

explanation.surface: A man who has enjoyed a lasting partnership in a local game.
explanation.walkthrough: Darby and Joan are the proverbial devoted elderly couple; in Britain 'derby' is said 'darby'.
explanation.definitionFit: Darby, of Darby and Joan, is the archetypal husband in a long, happy marriage.

clue.text: Collapse, divided by new dispute

indicators.note: the word for collapse is split, the letter for new sitting in between

parts.note: ruin means collapse

explanation.surface: A building collapses, and a new argument splits people.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is a quarrel or confrontation.

clue.text: A tramp is a kind of ship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a vagrant who drifts from place to place
second meaning: a fishing boat using drift nets

explanation.walkthrough: A tramp is also a kind of cargo ship, which tempts a single nautical meaning; here each half is its own sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A wandering vagrant is a drifter, and a drift-net fishing vessel bears the same name.

clue.text: Admit attempt by a Labour leader is gift for opposition

parts.note: to own is to admit or confess
a go is an attempt

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A Labour leader's admission hands the opposition an easy win.
explanation.walkthrough: In football an own goal is one scored into your own net.
explanation.definitionFit: An own goal benefits the rival side, figuratively any self-inflicted blunder that helps opponents.

clue.text: Elaborate and ornate style, as a rule

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the decorative fashion of Britain's ... period, 1811-20
second meaning: government by a regent

explanation.walkthrough: Regency style is the elegant architecture and furniture of early 19th-century Britain, named after the Prince Regent's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by a regent is a regency, and the period gave its name to a decorative manner of design.

clue.text: Scots knew why, it's said, this leader was slain

parts.note: in Scots, ken means know, so kenned means knew

indicators.note: it's said means the word is spoken, giving a letter of the same sound

parts.note: the word said aloud, sounding like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Scots understood the reason a leader was assassinated.
explanation.definitionFit: President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas in 1963.
